ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog is brown with a distinct dark hourglass pattern on its back. It features two prominent, light-colored spots near the groin and lacks toe discs. It belongs to family Ranixalidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Walkerana diplosticta* is uniquely identified by the presence of a distinct, bright white spot located on each side of its chest, just above the forelimb insertion.
ai.habitat: The Spotted Leaping Frog inhabits primary evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its powerful hind legs to perform long, rapid leaps into nearby water when threatened by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Walkerana diplosticta* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in terrestrial nests near streams, which undergo direct development without a tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Spotted Leaping Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Spotted Leaping Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
